newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay blue chips end lower after buoyant opening.
newsitem.headline: Bombay blue chips end lower after buoyant opening.

text.p: Bombay shares retreated by close on Monday as lack of follow-up buying from foreign funds prompted speculators to unwind positions in pivotal stocks, dealers said.
Trading volumes were lacklustre in most counters, they said.
"Early expectations of buying support didn't come up..there was not enough insitutional support," said Govind Agarwal, institutional dealer at brokerage Motilal Oswal.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) ended 36.46 points, or 1.07 percent lower at 3,385.89, off 3,478.0, the intra-day high.
Dealers said high carry-forward rates -- the charge of carrying transactions from one settlement to another -- weighed heavy on the minds of market participants.
Carry-forward rates leapt to an annualised 40-45 percent on Saturday at the BSE against 15-17 percent a week ago.
"This (carry-forward charges) indicated that people were holding long positions," said R. Ramakrishnan, chief dealer at ASK-Raymond James Securities India Ltd.
He said speculative selling in major stocks erased the market's early gains forcing the index to finish lower.
"Monday was more of an operators' day."
Dena Bank, the first in a series of Indian state-run banks to launch new issues, was listed on Monday and traded below its issue price, dealers said.
Shares of Dena Bank closed at 28 rupees at the BSE. The bank raised 1.8 billion rupees in November through an initial public offer at 30 rupees a share.
SBI lost 5.25 rupees to 272.75 rupees, TISCO 2.25 to 187.75, ACC 52.20 to 1,370.0, Reliance 3.0 to 235.75, L&T 15.50 to 231.25, BSES 9.25 to 211.25 and Bajaj Auto 29.75 to 892.0.
